newsitem.title: ITALY: INA to buy one pct of SanPaolo. [corrected 10:00 gmt 9/4]
newsitem.headline: INA to buy one pct of SanPaolo. [corrected 10:00 gmt 9/4]

text.p: (Corrects earlier story headlined "IMI to buy one pct of San Paolo". IMI has not said it will buy a one percent stake in San Paolo. The company in question was in fact Italian insurer INA. IMI is still pursuing negotiations which could lead to its becoming a core shareholder in San Paolo.)

Italian insurance group INA said on Tuesday night it had decided to buy a one percent stake in Italy's largest banking group Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino as part of the Turin-based bank's privatisation plan.
An INA statement said after a board meeting it would hold the shares for a "stabilisation period" of six months as a short-term financial investment in the banking sector.
However, the decision did not constitute a participation of INA in a proposed core shareholding group for the Turin bank, it said.
INA said the investment was part of its portfolio diversification policy and should be considered as "an interesting investment opportunity."
It said the price of the stake would be linked to the conditions foreseen for participants in San Paolo's expected public sale offer.
Earlier on Tuesday, investment bank IMI said it had empowered its executive comittee to pursue negotiations which could lead to it becoming a core shareholder of San Paolo.
IMI said the executive committee had been granted authority to carry on talks "aimed at the participation of the institute in agreements of stability ahead of the privatisation."
IMI currently holds a two percent stake in San Paolo with an option expiring in June to raise its stake to five percent and become a stable shareholder in San Paolo.
San Paolo, indirectly controlled by a foundation called Compagnia San Paolo, is moving ahead with plans to privatise ownership of the bank.
